patch_description:
This combines the direct-demand signal with a second-order path-coverage reward: a pair of selected links earns credit for carrying traffic that could otherwise require a direct link. To avoid giving every possible two-hop route the full value of the same demand, the path reward is shared across the four routes an OD pair could use under degree-two constraints.

The novel calibration uses maximum-normalized incident traffic to discount busy transit nodes, with a bounded inverse pressure factor. It also discounts routes whose component links already have substantial direct demand, since those links may have less spare capacity. A small endpoint-throughput contribution in the linear terms preserves useful source and destination signals without displacing direct demand.
